complexity.notes: Flattening with sum(..., []) re-copies the accumulated prefix for every group, so the pass costs O(n^2/k) overall (worst at k=1); a single loop or itertools.chain.from_iterable would make this same array approach linear. The statement permits modifying only next pointers, but this rebuilds the list from copied values in freshly allocated nodes; ||reversing each group in place by rewiring pointers|| would respect that rule and drop the extra space to O(1). Minor style: iterate `for v in a` instead of range(0, len(a)).
complexity.summary: Copies all node values into a Python list, reverses each complete block of k via slicing, concatenates the blocks with sum(..., []), then builds a brand-new linked list from the result.
